newsitem.title: USA: Miami health employees face Medicare fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: Miami health employees face Medicare fraud charges.

text.p: Twelve employees of a Miami healthcare company, Mederi of Dade County, have been charged with Medicare fraud in a case prosecutors described Thursday as one of the nation's largest home health scams.
Prosecutors said the defendants included two former administrators at the company and five doctors.

The administrators, Susan Regueiro and Leopoldo Perez, were accused of creating a network of phony nursing home groups and using them to submit bills to Medicare for patients who did not need, and often did not receive, home health treatment.
They funneled the proceeds back to themselves "through a maze of fictitious owners, corporate entities and bank accounts," said Willy Fernandez, a spokesman for the U.S. attorney's office in Miami.
"The indictment is the nation's single largest home health care fraud indictment ever returned by a federal grand jury," Fernandez said.

The indictment contains 102 counts of fraud, conspiracy and money laundering stemming from $15 million worth of allegedly fraudulent Medicare billings. Fernandez said the actual dollar amount of the alleged fraud was not known.
"It's just a small fraction of a much larger case that we're still working on," Fernandez said.
He said prosecutors were forced to seek an indictment before the investigation was finished because it was feared Regueiro would flee the country. She was arrested last week.
Five other suspects were arrested on Thursday and six made arrangements to turn themselves in, FBI spokeswoman Ann Figueiras said.
Attorney General Janet Reno said the charges stemmed from an ongoing crackdown of abuses in the federal Medicare program, which helps pay health costs for the aged, blind and disabled.
"Today's indictments are the latest examples of the success we are having in investigating health care fraud," Reno said in a statement.
A Mederi employee referred questions to an attorney, who was not immediately available for comment.
